{"claims":[{"claim_text":"To switch a running server from RDB to AOF, enable AOF on the live server with CONFIG SET appendonly yes.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 says to convert the data by enabling AOF via CONFIG on the live server first; passage 1 gives the exact command.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"If you want to enable AOF in a server that is currently using RDB snapshots, you need to convert the data by enabling AOF via CONFIG command on the live server first."},{"index":1,"quote":"Enable AOF: `redis-cli config set appendonly yes`"}]},{"claim_text":"Also update redis.conf.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 explicitly instructs updating redis.conf.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"**IMPORTANT:** Update your `redis.conf` (potentially through `CONFIG REWRITE`) and ensure that it matches the configuration above."}]},{"claim_text":"Otherwise the change is lost when the server restarts.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 states configuration changes are lost on restart if this step is forgotten.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"If you forget this step, when you restart the server, the configuration changes will be lost and the server will start again with the old configuration, resulting in a loss of your data."}]},{"claim_text":"Redis automatically blocks incoming writes while it converts the dataset.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passages do not state that Redis automatically blocks writes during conversion; one older procedure instructs the operator to stop all writes manually.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"Before restarting, wait until aof_rewrite_in_progress and aof_rewrite_scheduled are both 0.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 gives exactly these fields and value to wait for before restart.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"Before restarting the server, wait for AOF rewrite to finish persisting the data. You can do that by watching `INFO persistence`, waiting for `aof_rewrite_in_progress` and `aof_rewrite_scheduled` to be `0`"}]},{"claim_text":"On Redis 7.0 or later, an AOF-only instance can be backed up by copying the files in a directory.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 says AOF-only instances can be backed up, and since 7.0.0 the AOF files are in a single directory that can be copied/tarred.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"Since Redis 7.0.0, AOF files are split into multiple files which reside in a single directory determined by the `appenddirname` configuration."},{"index":4,"quote":"During normal operation all you need to do is copy/tar the files in this directory to achieve a backup."}]},{"claim_text":"That directory is set by the appendfilename option.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 says the directory is determined by appenddirname, not appendfilename.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"Since Redis 7.0.0, AOF files are split into multiple files which reside in a single directory determined by the `appenddirname` configuration."}]},{"claim_text":"Copying the files while a rewrite is running is safe.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 says copying during a rewrite might produce an invalid backup and rewrites must be disabled during backup.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"However, if this is done during a [rewrite](#log-rewriting), you might end up with an invalid backup."},{"index":4,"quote":"To work around this you must disable AOF rewrites during the backup:"}]},{"claim_text":"To be extra careful you can set auto-aof-rewrite-percentage to 0, which turns off automatic rewrites.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 instructs turning off automatic rewrites with auto-aof-rewrite-percentage 0.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"Turn off automatic rewrites with
`CONFIG SET` `auto-aof-rewrite-percentage 0`"}]},{"claim_text":"If you take hard links to those files, you can re-enable rewrites before the copy finishes.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 says to create hard links, then re-enable rewrites, and then copy/tar the hardlinks.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"you may create hard links to the files in `appenddirname` (in step 3 above) and then re-enable rewrites (step 4) after the hard links are created. Now you can copy/tar the hardlinks and delete them when done."}]},{"claim_text":"Redis only appends to files in that directory or completely replaces them.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 states Redis guarantees this behavior, which is why hard-link backups work.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"This works because Redis guarantees that it only appends to files in this directory, or completely replaces them if necessary"}]},{"claim_text":"On Redis 6.0, backing up the AOF is as simple as copying the aof file.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 7 says prior to version 7.0.0 the AOF can be backed up simply by copying the aof file; Redis 6.0 is prior to 7.0.0.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"Prior to version 7.0.0 backing up the AOF file can be done simply by copying the aof file (like backing up the RDB snapshot)."}]},{"claim_text":"Redis can still load the copy even if it lacks the final part.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 7 says the file may lack the final part but Redis will still load it.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"The file may lack the final part but Redis will still be able to load it"}]}]}
